newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries closing narrowly range bound.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries closing narrowly range bound.

text.p: Prices of U.S. Treasury securities were closing narrowly mixed Thursday amid a dearth of significant news ahead of next week's economic reports.

The market retained its positive tone in the wake of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat assessment on the U.S. economy before Congress on Tuesday. Durable goods orders for June were scheduled for release on Friday, but that figure -- notoriously volatile -- was not expected to have much market impact. Instead, market players were looking forward to the release of employment data next Tuesday.
The Employment Cost Index (ECI) for the second quarter of 1997 was scheduled for release on Tuesday and players said no significant movement in bond prices was expected before then.

"The bond market is going to be fine in the near term. I don't see anything on the radar screen to shatter (that optimistic scenario)," said Anthony Karadakis, senior financial economist at First National Bank of Chicago.
Karadakis said aircraft orders would likely lift durable goods orders at least 1.0 percent, but further tightening by the Federal Reserve may not occur until the end of the year.
Durable goods orders were expected to have risen 1.4 percent in June, economists surveyed by Reuters said, reversing the 0.7 percent decline seen in May.
Economists looked to a rise of at least 1.0 percent, but tempered that prediction by noting the series was notoriously volatile.
Most saw the figure being propped up by aircraft orders in the quarter.
"We're talking about a modest gain of 1.0 percent, which pushes durable goods back into a modestly upward trend," said Karadakis, at First National Bank of Chicago.

Economists said a bounce-back could be expected in orders following the prior month's weak performance. If the transportation sector was excluded, however, most saw only a 1.0 percent rise in durable goods orders.
Before the release of next week's economic data, economists said the bond market was comfortable at current levels and prices were unlikely to move much in either direction.

The Treasury's 30-year bond was closing up 2/32 at 102-18/32 to yield 6.43 percent. Three-month bills were two basis points higher at 5.08 percent. Six-month bills were up one basis point at 5.13 percent and year bills were down one basis point at 5.22 percent.

The 10-year issue was unchanged at 103-14/32 to yield 6.15 percent. The five-year note was also unchanged at 99-24/32 yielding 6.06 percent. The two-year note was up 1/32 at 100-1/32 to yield 5.86 percent.
